title: Traefik explicit priority overriding specificity (preserve or refuse)
claims: an explicit higher priority on the broader rule keeps /p/q/x on the broad router's backend
the broad router serves its other paths
not_claimed: priority ties, negative priorities, and cross-entryPoint ordering
source_semantics: Traefik evaluates routers by priority (explicit values override the rule-length default), so r-broad (100) shadows r-narrow (1) for /p/q/x. Ferrum's longest-prefix rule would choose the narrow route, so the converter must preserve this ordering or refuse with a report error.
